subject: ocean sunfish
title: One Fish Releases 300 Million Eggs at Once, More Than Any Animal

scenes.text: One fish. One spawning. 300 million eggs.
It's the ocean sunfish, a swimming head the size of a car. It is the heaviest bony fish on Earth.
A female scatters up to 300 million eggs into open water, more than any other backboned animal. Each egg is 1.3 millimetres wide, smaller than a grain of rice.
The larvae hatch as spiky little balls, go through three strange stages, and almost all of them get eaten.
The survivors grow for years. In 2021, one washed up in the Azores at 2,744 kilograms, nearly three tons, and 3.6 metres tall.
From a 1.3 millimetre egg to three tons. When a fish starts that small, it can afford to start 300 million times.

description:
An ocean sunfish can release up to 300 million eggs in a single spawning, more than any other vertebrate.
Each egg is about 1.3 millimetres across; the larvae pass through three spiny stages and the few survivors become the heaviest bony fish alive. The record is a giant sunfish found dead off the Azores in December 2021: 2,744 kilograms and about 3.6 metres tall (Journal of Fish Biology, 2022).
Would you rather have 300 million eggs or one big baby?
first_comment: Sunfish lie flat at the surface to warm up after deep dives, and seabirds land on them to pick off parasites. Which ocean giant should we cover next?
